chunks: Safwan ibn Yahya narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who shot game in the Ḥill while heading toward the Haram, in the area between the post station and the mosque. He struck it in the Ḥill, then it continued from that shot until it entered the Haram and died from his shot. Is there a penalty upon him?

He عليه السلام said: "There is no penalty upon him. The likeness of that is only like one who sets a trap in the Ḥill beside the Haram, then game falls into it and struggles until it enters the Haram and dies. Then its penalty is not upon him, because he set it where he set it while that was halal for him, and he shot where he shot while that was halal for him; so there is nothing upon him regarding what occurred after that."
I said: "This is qiyas according to the people." He عليه السلام said: "I only compared one thing to another for you so that you may recognize it."

key_terms.الْحَرَمَ: the sacred sanctuary in which hunting is prohibited
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: the area outside the sacred sanctuary where hunting is ordinarily halal
key_terms.الْقِيَاسُ: analogy; here mentioned in contrast to the Imam’s explanatory comparison
key_terms.جَزَاءٌ: the legal compensation or penalty due for unlawful killing of game
key_terms.حَلَالٌ: legally permissible in that location and circumstance
key_terms.شَبَّهْتُ: I compared; used by the Imam to clarify the ruling through resemblance
key_terms.شَرَكًا: a trap set for catching game

ai.seo_question: Is a hunter liable if he strikes game in the Ḥill and it later dies inside the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about hunting near the boundary of the Haram: if the act of striking or trapping the game occurred lawfully in the Ḥill, no penalty is due if the animal later enters the Haram and dies there. The Imam عليه السلام also clarifies that his comparison is explanatory, not qiyas as used by others.
